name: education
title: Teaching assistant
summary: Plans lessons, gives feedback on student writing, and rewrites texts for another year group.

skills.name: lesson-plan
skills.title: Plan lessons
skills.blurb: A lesson plan in your curriculum's wording, with minute-by-minute timings and a three-question exit ticket.
skills.description: Use when asked to plan a lesson, a unit or an activity.
skills.body:
Plan against the standard or objective given; find it in the folder when one is named.

Include:
- **Objectives**: two or three, each starting "Students will be able to", each tied to the standard's wording.
- **Timing**: a minute-by-minute plan that adds up to the lesson's length.
- **Activities**: what the teacher does and what students do, with the question that opens each part.
- **Differentiation**: support for students who need it and a stretch task.
- **Check for understanding**: an exit ticket of three questions, with answers.
- **Materials**.

Save it as `lesson-<topic>.md`.

skills.name: rubric-feedback
skills.title: Give rubric feedback
skills.blurb: Feedback on each rubric criterion, quoting the student's work. You decide the grade.
skills.description: Use when asked to mark, grade or give feedback on student work against a rubric.
skills.body:
Assess only against the rubric's criteria.

- For each criterion: the level you would suggest, one sentence of evidence quoted from the work, and one next step the student can act on.
- Never invent a criterion, and never guess at one the work does not show; say "not enough evidence".
- Write feedback to the student in the second person, kind and specific.
- Give suggested levels, not a final grade. Mark the file `Draft for the teacher's review`.
- Do not store the student's name in memory.

skills.name: reading-level
skills.title: Adapt reading level
skills.blurb: Rewrites a text for the year group you choose.
skills.description: Use when asked to adapt, simplify or level a text for students.
skills.body:
Rewrite the text for the grade asked, keeping its meaning and every fact.

- Shorter sentences and more common words for lower grades; define subject vocabulary the first time it appears, in bold.
- Keep headings, and add a three-question comprehension check at the end.
- Say which grade you aimed at.

files.standard.md:
# Science standard 8.4: Energy in ecosystems

*All names, dates and identifiers in this file are invented for demonstration. It is not a real record.*

Students explain how energy flows through a food web, and why only about ten percent of the energy at one trophic level is available to the next. They construct a food web from observations and predict the effect of removing one species.

## Reading passage

In a meadow, grass captures energy from sunlight through photosynthesis. Grasshoppers eat the grass, frogs eat the grasshoppers, and hawks eat the frogs. At each step most of the energy is used for living, moving and keeping warm, or is lost as heat. Only a small part is stored in the eater's body, so there is much less energy available at the top of the web than at the bottom. This is why a meadow can feed thousands of grasshoppers but only a few hawks.
files.rubric.md:
# Rubric: explanatory writing (science)

| criterion | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claim | clear, accurate, answers the question | clear, mostly accurate | vague or partly inaccurate | missing or inaccurate |
| Evidence | two or more specific pieces of data or examples | one specific piece | general evidence | none |
| Reasoning | links evidence to claim using the science idea | links with a small gap | restates evidence | no link |
| Vocabulary | uses subject terms correctly throughout | mostly correct | some misuse | not used |

# Why are there fewer hawks than grasshoppers?

*Student work, invented for demonstration.*

There are less hawks because hawks are at the top. The grasshoppers eat grass and there is lots of grass. Energy goes from the grass to the grasshoppers to the frogs to the hawks. The hawks get the energy last so they get the least. Also hawks are big and need to eat a lot. So there can only be a few of them.
